outcome: cesarean scar sonographic healing (niche formation, healing ratio)
cesarean scar location (relative to internal cervical os)
cohort: Women who underwent cesarean delivery during active labor (cervical dilation 4-10 cm) at the University College London Hospital.
finding: Advanced cervical dilatation and low fetal station at emergency cesarean delivery in labor independently predict cesarean scar location near or within the cervix, and these cervical scars exhibit poorer healing compared to those higher in the uterus.
mod_finding: Advanced cervical dilatation and low fetal station during emergency cesarean delivery in labor are associated with a higher likelihood of the cesarean scar being located near or within the cervix, which is linked to less optimal scar healing.
gest_age: Measured as a factor influencing scar healing
